analysis: Examined ClusterPlacementPlanner.swift: base lines 885-1324 (tensorRequirement, ordering, prediction helpers) and head lines 1-467 (policy structs, plan() entry validation). The visible change is a placement-ranking policy tweak. A family whose plan has `choosesFastest` (fastestOnly) now ignores `tensorParallelFirst` and is ranked by speed comparison. For such families, an unmeasured link is priced with `ClusterTensorParallelChoice.assumedReduction` rather than `assumingForcedReduction()`. This is local scheduling and performance logic: it is a pure function with no clock, I/O, crypto, attestation, authorization or data exposure. It is outside the retained threat model assets (A-001..A-019, T-041 prefix cache, TB-002/TB-007/TB-011/TB-012/TB-013), and I found no regression against it. Input validation in plan() is unchanged and still bounds device labels (utf8 count at most 64, distinct), context and prompt/output ranges, requiredTensorShares, and the assistant quote preconditions. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the new `ClusterTensorParallelChoice`, `choosesFastest` and `link.assuming(...)` definitions are outside the supplied evidence. The head text is cut at line 467, and the later changes (head ranges 637-643, near the base 630/632 changes) are not visible in the supplied units. I could not verify them, so I cannot conclude they are safe. Residual question: whether those unseen edits alter memory-fit gates (tensorRequirement, requirement) in a way that over-admits load or request memory. That would be an availability concern for an OOM-prone provider, not a confidentiality concern. Nothing in the visible lines touches key handling, plaintext prompts, or the coordinator wire contract.
